owner: Hyperreal native exact atan/pi correspondences and pi/atan trig argument recognition
proof_argument: The shared anchor correspondence is atan(1)=pi/4, atan(sqrt(3))=pi/3, atan(1/sqrt(3))=pi/6, with positive principal arguments and odd arctangent symmetry. Forward construction retains its previous graph shape.

The native reader first proves the expression has zero rational offset and no surviving atan term or argument, retaining only q*pi. It accepts q only when its normalized denominator is 3, 4 or 6. No approximate sample determines this branch.

For |q|=k+f with integer k and 0<f<1, parity of k changes both trig signs; reflection f to 1-f changes only cosine; negating q changes only sine. In the accepted reduced denominators, the reflected positive fraction is exactly 1/3, 1/4 or 1/6.

The recovered positive argument is consumed by the existing native pair a/sqrt(1+a*a), 1/sqrt(1+a*a), with the proven sine/cosine signs. The existing half-pi machinery and source angle graphs are retained.
The Real-facing reader requests its original accepted forms. This avoids replacing the already-supported canonical Real trig path, as checked by 532 unchanged public JSON/CBOR output rows.
negative_controls: Nonzero rational offsets, including 2^-512, cannot satisfy the required zero constant term.
Other reduced denominators and non-unit atan coefficients retain their existing paths.
Raw invalid numeric domains and imported undefined children remain covered by the previous domain suites.
resource_scope: Reuse the already-present depth-64 pi/atan linear form, without recursive calls from atan_argument back into pi/Laurent recognition. Exact denominator inspection uses checked integer conversion, never a floating-point estimate. Existing coefficient growth, total work, native cancellation and allocation are not fully bounded internally; fixed external containment remains necessary.
source_and_serialization: Only newly derived native trig outputs intentionally migrate to existing algebraic tags. Forty-eight captured prior native JSON graphs are re-encoded as CBOR as well as imported from JSON for consumption checks; these are not represented as historical native CBOR byte captures. Public source-angle serialization is compared to the pre-edit capture.
